The same managed app configuration Okta Verify itself reads, delivered to its authentication service extension.
Okta requires both domains to carry the configuration. Build it once for com.okta.mobile, then deliver the identical dictionary here; a device that has one and not the other fails device trust in ways that look like an Okta policy problem.
Configures the Okta Verify authentication service extension
The human-readable description of this payload. This description appears on the Detail screen.
The human-readable name for the profile payload. The name appears on the Detail screen and doesn’t need to be unique.

The reverse-DNS-style identifier for the payload. This identifier is usually the same as the TopLevel value, with an additional appended component. This string must be unique within the profile. During a profile replacement, the system updates payloads with the same ‘PayloadIdentifier’ and ‘PayloadUUID’ in the old and new profiles.
The payload type, which each payload domain’s reference page specifies.

The globally unique identifier for the payload. The actual content is unimportant, but must be globally unique. In macOS, use ‘uuidgen’ to generate UUIDs. During a profile replacement, the system updates payloads with the same ‘PayloadIdentifier’ and ‘PayloadUUID’ in the old and new profiles.
The version of this specific payload.
The human-readable string containing the name of the organization that provides the profile. This value doesn’t need to match the organization payload value in the enclosing dictionary.

Your Okta org’s sign-in URL, pre-filled so the user does not have to type it during enrolment.
Enter the hostname on its own — for example example.okta.com.
Shared secret that tells Okta this device is managed. It must match the secret key configured on the Okta side of the device management integration.
This value is a credential, and it is what device-trust policies rest on. Deliver it in an encrypted profile, never in a plain-text profile committed to source control.

Device serial number, so Okta can match the device to your inventory.
Use your MDM’s serial-number variable — $SERIALNUMBER in Jamf Pro, {{serialnumber}} in Intune.
Serial numbers are only readable on supervised devices. Okta Verify reports an empty value where the platform withholds it, which is not an error.

Unique device identifier, so Okta can match the device to your inventory.
Use $UDID in Jamf Pro or {{$UDID}} in Intune. For user-enrolment scenarios use the management ID variable instead — $MANAGEMENTID.
Whether Okta Verify collects diagnostic data, including non-fatal errors.
Whether console logs are included when the app crashes.
Whether performance metrics are gathered for troubleshooting.
Whether users can submit feedback and bug reports from inside the app.
Whether users can save logs locally and export them from the Send feedback menu.
